senses.gloss: m.(b. h.;תהם , Friedr. Del. Proleg., p. 113) deep, depth, interior of the earth.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 2:4">Gen. R. s. 2</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 1:2">Gen. I, 2</cite>) <he>זו מלכות … כמו הת׳</he> ‘the deep’, that is the wicked (Roman) empire which is unfathomable as the deep; <he>מה הת׳ הזה וכ׳</he> as the deep cannot be searched out, so the wicked &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah 2:1:13">Y. Ḥag. II, 77ᶜ</cite> <he>מה … ומה למטה מן הת׳</he> what is above the heavens, and what is beneath the deep.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 97b:4">Snh. 97ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="N01155"><he>נָקַב</he></cite>; a. fr.—<he>קבר הת׳</he>, <he>טומאת הת׳</he> a grave in the depth, i.e. a covered up uncleanness discovered.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 9:2:7">Y. Naz. IX, 57ᵈ</cite> top <he>אי זה הוא קבר הת׳ המת שנקבר וכ׳</he> what is a grave of the depth (in a legal sense)? A corpse buried in stubble, straw, earth, or pebbles, but if buried in water &c., it does not make a grave of the depth (does not make unclean that which was above it before discovery).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 9:2:7">Ib.</cite> <he>אי זהו קבר הת׳ … זוכרו</he> a grave of the depth is one that nobody remembers to have existed; a. fr.—Pl. <he>תְּהוֹמוֹת</he>. Mekh. B’shall., Shir., s. 5, v. <cite ref="P01470"><he>עִשּׁוֹנִית</he></cite>; a. e.
